answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake in a vault before transacting, slashed if peers prove duplicate or fraudulent behaviour. A newcomer starts in a narrow canyon of permissions, low-value trades only, widening only after completed work and peer attestations accumulate. One whisper of suspicion triggers no ban, but a verified report triggers an audit costing the attacker its stake and reputation, so flooding the network with thousands of fakes means funding thousands of stakes, making Sybil attacks linearly expensive, not free.
